regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Telluride leads the region with 14" of total snow, peaking Sunday at 11". NWS calls for rain and snow showers Sunday, with a slight chance of thunderstorms, then snow showers Monday (2 to 4 inches possible), and a Winter Storm Watch is in effect. Crested Butte is forecast for 7" and Aspen Highlands for 5", with 4" of that at Aspen on Monday. A Winter Weather Advisory covers Crested Butte.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Wolf Creek has 13" of total snow, with 12" falling Sunday. NWS notes rain and snow showers Sunday, with snow showers and gusts to 45 mph, and a Winter Storm Watch is in effect. Taos is forecast for 4" total, with 2" Sunday and 2" Monday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Grand Targhee leads with 7" total, all of it forecast for Sunday. NWS calls for rain and snow showers Saturday night, then snow showers Sunday (less than one inch possible), followed by 1 to 2 inches Sunday night. Jackson Hole is forecast for 6", with 5" on Sunday, and Big Sky for 3".

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth is forecast for 6" total, all falling Saturday. NWS calls for heavy snow Saturday and Saturday night, with 8 to 12 inches possible overnight, and wind chill values as low as 14. A Winter Weather Advisory is in effect. Snow is likely again Sunday, with 1 to 2 inches possible.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Alta leads with 6" total, peaking Sunday at 5". NWS calls for heavy snow Sunday and Sunday night, with 9 to 13 inches possible Sunday and 10 to 14 inches Sunday night. Snowbird and Brighton are both forecast for 6" total, with Snowbird's Sunday night snow at 6 to 10 inches possible.

ahead.text: The Climate Prediction Center is not in the discussions provided, so nothing here. The Weather Prediction Center's extended outlook shows snow likely over higher Rockies elevations early next week, with an active pattern and Pacific energy reaching the West Coast by midweek, though its confidence drops after Monday.
